steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Carbohydrates are the body's main source of energy. They are divided into sugars (simple, quick-release) and starches (complex, slow-release). Excess glucose is stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles, or converted to fat. | Key Fact: Proteins are essential for growth, repair, and maintenance of body tissues. They are made up of amino acids — there are 20 amino acids, 9 of which are essential (cannot be synthesised by the body and must come from food). | Key Fact: High biological value (HBV) proteins contain all 9 essential amino acids — found in animal sources (meat, fish, eggs, dairy) and soya. Low biological value (LBV) proteins lack one or more essential amino acids — found in plant sources (cereals, pulses, nuts). | Key Fact: Complementary proteins: combining LBV protein
